hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 undergoes increased aggregation in the endo-lysosome compared with APOE3.

rows.Finding description: Deleting residues 1–71 produced a more complicated and aggregated sedimentation distribution for recombinant apoE4-(72–299) than for apoE3-(72–299) in PBS.
rows.Finding quote: Compared with the simplicity in size distribution of apoE3-(72–299), apoE4-(72–299) existed in a more complicated and aggregated pattern (Fig. 1C).
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3-(72–299) -> apoE4-(72–299)) -> (greater apoE self-aggregation in PBS)
rows.Experimental system: Purified recombinant human apoE3-(72–299) and apoE4-(72–299), expressed in E. coli BL21(DE3), with C-terminal tags; 0.5 mg/ml in PBS, pH 7.3; sedimentation velocity at 20 °C and 42,000 rpm for 3.5 h; continuous c(s) analysis. Cell-free, non-acidic system.

rows.Finding description: In PBS, apoE4-(1–231) had a larger approximately tetrameric peak than apoE3-(1–231), 53% versus 42%, and a smaller approximately monomeric peak, 29% versus 43%.
rows.Finding quote: ApoE3-(1–231) proteins maintained more monomer, but apoE4-(1–231) had more tet- ramer.
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3-(1–231) -> apoE4-(1–231)) -> (greater tetramer representation and lower monomer representation in PBS)
rows.Experimental system: Purified recombinant human apoE3-(1–231) and apoE4-(1–231), expressed in E. coli BL21(DE3), with C-terminal tags; 0.5 mg/ml in PBS, pH 7.3; sedimentation velocity at 20 °C and 42,000 rpm for 3.5 h; continuous c(s) analysis. Cell-free, non-acidic system.
rows.Data location: Fig 1D; Results, Self-aggregation of ApoE Proteins Determined by Size Distribution Analysis

rows.Finding description: A single-species sedimentation-equilibrium fit gave apoE4-(72–166) a higher equivalent molar mass than apoE3-(72–166) in PBS, 429 versus 187 kDa.
rows.Finding quote: The most significant difference between apoE3 and apoE4 isoform is their corresponding apoE-(72–166) proteins, which have a Meq of 187 kDa for apoE3-(72– 166) and 429 kDa for apoE4-(72–166).
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3-(72–166) -> apoE4-(72–166)) -> (higher equivalent molar mass in PBS)
rows.Experimental system: Purified recombinant human apoE3-(72–166) and apoE4-(72–166), expressed in E. coli BL21(DE3); 0.5 mg/ml in PBS, pH 7.3; sedimentation equilibrium at 20 °C, four speeds from 6,000 to 20,000 rpm, each for 14 h; single-species SEDPHAT fit. The theoretical tagged monomer mass was 12 kDa.
rows.Data location: Table 1, ApoE3-(72–166) and ApoE4-(72–166) rows, Mass in PBS column

rows.Finding description: Global discrete-species fitting resolved a broader, larger aggregate population for apoE4-(72–299), including a largest fitted species of 666 kDa versus 351 kDa for apoE3-(72–299).
rows.Finding quote: ApoE3-(72–299) main- tained a major species of tetramer (by SV) or hexamer (by SE), and apoE4-(72–299) showed a complicated distribution of tetramer (or tri- mer), octamer, decamer, 14-mer, and large aggregates.
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3-(72–299) -> apoE4-(72–299)) -> (broader apoE oligomer distribution containing larger aggregates)
rows.Experimental system: Purified recombinant human apoE3-(72–299) and apoE4-(72–299) in aqueous PBS, pH 7.3; global analysis of sedimentation-equilibrium and sedimentation-velocity data at 20 °C; four discrete species fitted for apoE3-(72–299) and six for apoE4-(72–299).

rows.Finding description: The Results report more large aggregates for apoE4-(72–166) in aqueous PBS. Table 2 separately gives the highest fitted species masses as 632 kDa for apoE4-(72–166) and 243 kDa for apoE3-(72–166).
rows.Finding quote: ApoE4-(72–166) maintained more large aggregates in aqueous PBS.
rows.Finding summary: ApoE4-(72–166) showed more large aggregates than apoE3-(72–166) in aqueous PBS.
rows.Experimental system: Purified recombinant human apoE3-(72–166) and apoE4-(72–166), expressed in E. coli BL21(DE3); aqueous PBS, pH 7.3; combined sedimentation-equilibrium and sedimentation-velocity analysis at 20 °C using four discrete species per isoform.

rows.Finding description: Additional global sedimentation analyses are cited collectively in Supplementary Figs 3S–8S, while the main text reports more tetramer for apoE4-(1–231) and more monomer for apoE3-(1–231); the specific supplementary figure and panel assignments are unavailable.
rows.Finding quote: ApoE3-(1–231) proteins maintained more monomer, but apoE4-(1–231) had more tet- ramer.
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3-(1–231) -> apoE4-(1–231)) -> (greater tetramer representation in PBS)
rows.Experimental system: Purified recombinant human apoE3-(1–231) and apoE4-(1–231) in aqueous PBS; combined sedimentation-equilibrium and sedimentation-velocity analysis using SEDPHAT. Supplementary data and legends were unavailable; no construct-to-figure mapping was assumed.
rows.Data location: Table 2, ApoE-(1–231) rows, especially the SV local concentrations for the monomer and tetramer. Supplementary Figs. 3S–8S are cited collectively, with the individual panel unavailable.

rows.Finding description: A single-species sedimentation-equilibrium fit gave apoE4-(72–299) a higher equivalent molar mass than apoE3-(72–299) in PBS, 209 versus 192 kDa.
rows.Finding quote: The apoE3-(72–299) and apoE4-(72–299) proteins exhibited a Meq of 192 and 209 kDa, respectively.
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3-(72–299) -> apoE4-(72–299)) -> (higher equivalent molar mass in PBS)
rows.Experimental system: Purified recombinant human apoE3-(72–299) and apoE4-(72–299), expressed in E. coli BL21(DE3); 0.5 mg/ml in PBS, pH 7.3; sedimentation equilibrium at 20 °C, four speeds from 6,000 to 20,000 rpm, each for 14 h; single-species SEDPHAT fit to heterogeneous protein populations.
rows.Data location: Table 1, ApoE3-(72–299) and ApoE4-(72–299) rows, Mass in PBS column

rows.Finding description: A single-species sedimentation-equilibrium fit gave apoE4-(1–231) a lower equivalent molar mass than apoE3-(1–231) in PBS, 162 versus 205 kDa, opposite to increased aggregation by this measure.
rows.Finding quote: The apoE3-(1–231) and apoE4-(1–231) showed a Meq of 205 and 162 kDa, respectively.
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3-(1–231) -> apoE4-(1–231)) -> (lower equivalent molar mass in PBS)
rows.Experimental system: Purified recombinant human apoE3-(1–231) and apoE4-(1–231), expressed in E. coli BL21(DE3); 0.5 mg/ml in PBS, pH 7.3; sedimentation equilibrium at 20 °C, four speeds from 6,000 to 20,000 rpm, each for 14 h; single-species SEDPHAT fit to heterogeneous protein populations.
rows.Data location: Table 1, ApoE3-(1–231) and ApoE4-(1–231) rows, Mass in PBS column

rows.Finding description: With 50 mM DHPC, apoE3-(72–299) and apoE4-(72–299) became predominantly monomeric, with major low-sedimentation species comprising 65% and 75%, respectively; no significant difference in isoform-specific aggregation was reported or statistically tested.
rows.Finding quote: This isoformic structural variation did not exist in the presence of dihexanoylphosphatidylcholine.
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3-(72–299) -> apoE4-(72–299)) -> (no change in predominantly monomeric apoE state with DHPC)
rows.Experimental system: Purified recombinant human apoE3-(72–299) and apoE4-(72–299), expressed in E. coli BL21(DE3); 0.5 mg/ml in PBS, pH 7.3, containing 50 mM DHPC; sedimentation velocity at 20 °C and 42,000 rpm for 6 h; continuous c(s) analysis.

rows.Finding description: With 50 mM DHPC, apoE3-(72–299) and apoE4-(72–299) had monomer-like equivalent molar masses of 30 and 26 kDa, respectively, with no significant difference in oligomeric state reported or statistically tested.
rows.Finding quote: In the presence of DHPC, all kinds of apoE proteins maintained a Meq corresponding to their monomer molar mass (Table 1).
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3-(72–299) -> apoE4-(72–299)) -> (no change in monomeric apoE state with DHPC)
rows.Experimental system: Purified recombinant human apoE3-(72–299) and apoE4-(72–299); 0.5 mg/ml in PBS, pH 7.3, containing 50 mM DHPC; sedimentation equilibrium at 20 °C, four speeds from 6,000 to 20,000 rpm, each for 14 h; single-species SEDPHAT fit; theoretical monomer mass 27 kDa.
rows.Data location: Table 1, ApoE3-(72–299) and ApoE4-(72–299) rows, Mass in PBS containing 50 mM DHPC column

rows.Finding description: Full-length recombinant human apoE3 and apoE4 showed similar oligomer-size distributions in PBS, with no significant difference reported; an isoform-comparison significance test was not supplied.
rows.Finding quote: ApoE3 and apoE4 proteins showed the similar size distribution patterns by continuous c(s) size distribution analysis (Fig. 1B).
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (no change in overall full-length apoE oligomer-size distribution in PBS)
rows.Experimental system: Purified recombinant full-length human apoE3 and apoE4 expressed in E. coli BL21-CodonPlus(DE3)-RIPL, with C-terminal tags; 0.5 mg/ml in PBS, pH 7.3; sedimentation velocity at 20 °C and 42,000 rpm for 3.5 h; continuous c(s) analysis. No cells, brain tissue, aging condition, or endo-lysosomal localization was examined.

rows.Finding description: The fitted full-length apoE3 and apoE4 distributions both contained monomer, dimer, tetramer, hexamer, octamer, and decamer classes, with no significant difference in the overall oligomerization pattern reported or statistically tested.
rows.Finding quote: For apoE3 and apoE4 proteins, the discrete species of molar mass corresponded to monomer, dimer, tetramer, hexamer, octamer, and decamer.
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (no change in the broad classes of full-length apoE oligomers in PBS)
rows.Experimental system: Purified recombinant full-length human apoE3 and apoE4 in aqueous PBS; discrete species and local A280 concentrations estimated by global analysis of sedimentation-equilibrium and sedimentation-velocity experiments at 20 °C.

rows.Finding description: With 50 mM DHPC, full-length apoE3 and apoE4 became predominantly monomeric, with major low-sedimentation species comprising 79% and 73%, respectively; no significant difference in isoform-specific aggregation was reported or statistically tested.
rows.Finding quote: Each protein appeared as a major species at s  1.6–2.2 (79, 73, 65, 75, 85, and 64% for apoE3, apoE4, apoE3-(72–299), apoE4- (72–299), apoE3-(1–231), and apoE4-(1–231), respectively
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (no change in predominantly monomeric apoE state with DHPC)
rows.Experimental system: Purified recombinant full-length human apoE3 and apoE4 expressed in E. coli; 0.5 mg/ml in PBS, pH 7.3, containing 50 mM DHPC; sedimentation velocity at 20 °C and 42,000 rpm for 6 h; continuous c(s) analysis. The major species sedimented at 1.6–2.2 S across tested constructs.

rows.Finding description: The main text links Supplementary Fig 2S to monomer-like apoE in DHPC, with no significant difference in oligomeric state reported between isoforms; individual supplementary comparisons and statistics could not be inspected.
rows.Finding quote: In the presence of DHPC, all kinds of apoE proteins maintained a Meq corresponding to their monomer molar mass (Table 1). This indicated that a single spe- cies model is adequate to describe the apoE proteins in DHPC-contain- ing PBS (Fig. 2 and supplemental Fig. 2S).
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (no change in predominantly monomeric apoE state with DHPC)
rows.Experimental system: Purified recombinant human apoE proteins in PBS with DHPC; sedimentation-equilibrium experiments described in the main text. Supplementary Fig 2S and its legend were unavailable, preventing identification of individual construct-to-panel assignments.
rows.Data location: Table 1, paired apoE3 and apoE4 rows, theoretical monomer mass and mass in PBS containing 50 mM DHPC. Results also cites Supplementary Fig. 2S, whose individual panels are unavailable.

rows.Finding description: A single-species sedimentation-equilibrium fit gave full-length apoE4 a slightly higher equivalent molar mass than apoE3 in PBS, 158 versus 151 kDa.
rows.Finding quote: On the other hand, apoE3 and apoE4 showed a Meq of 151 and 158 kDa, respectively, in aqueous PBS.
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (slightly higher equivalent molar mass in PBS)
rows.Experimental system: Purified recombinant full-length human apoE3 and apoE4 expressed in E. coli; 0.5 mg/ml in PBS, pH 7.3; sedimentation equilibrium at 20 °C and 6,000, 10,000, 15,000, and 20,000 rpm, each for 14 h; single-species SEDPHAT fit to heterogeneous protein populations.
rows.Data location: Table 1, ApoE3 and ApoE4 rows, Mass in PBS column

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, for example astrocytes, APOE4 causes impaired ARF6-related recycling of receptors between the cell surface and the endosome, compared with APOE3.

rows.Finding description: Surface-biotinylated sortilin internalized in CHO-S cells exposed to apoE3 or apoE4. During recycling, dynasore blocked receptor re-entry. Recycling with apoE4 was 49.56 ± 16.92% versus 100 ± 13.84% with apoE3, normalized to the apoE3 mean (n = 9 biological replicates from three independent experiments).
rows.Finding quote: In these studies, the amount of receptors recycling back to the cell surface was reduced by 50% in apoE4-treated as com- pared to apoE3-treated cells (Figures 6D, E
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (reduced recycling of internalized sortilin to the cell surface)
rows.Experimental system: CHO cells stably expressing murine sortilin (CHO-S); 5 µg/mL apoE3 or apoE4; surface biotinylation at 4 °C, 15 min internalization at 37 °C, GSH strip, then 60 min recycling with dynasore and GSH strip; streptavidin pulldown and western blot densitometry

rows.Finding description: Antibody-labeled surface sortilin in CHO-S cells recycled back to the surface (seen in non-permeabilized cells after dynasore) with apoE3-conditioned medium, but stayed largely intracellular with apoE4-conditioned medium.
rows.Finding quote: The recycling path of sortilin established in CHO cells was not impacted by the presence of apoE3 in the culture medium (Figure 6B). However, in the presence of apoE4, internalized receptors failed to re-appear on the cell surface and remained largely intracellular (Fig- ure 6B
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (loss of sortilin re-appearance at the cell surface)
rows.Experimental system: CHO-S cells (murine sortilin) in apoE3- or apoE4-conditioned medium; surface antibody labeling at 4 °C, 15 min internalization at 37 °C, 60 min dynasore; immunocytochemistry of permeabilized vs non-permeabilized cells

rows.Finding description: Western blots of biotinylated sortilin pulled down on streptavidin after the internalization and recycling phases showed that more biotinylated receptor stayed intracellular with apoE4 than with apoE3, indicating less recycling.
rows.Finding quote: In these studies, the amount of receptors recycling back to the cell surface was reduced by 50% in apoE4-treated as com- pared to apoE3-treated cells (Figures 6D, E
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (more biotinylated sortilin retained intracellularly after recycling phase)
rows.Experimental system: CHO-S cells (murine sortilin); 5 µg/mL apoE3 or apoE4; biotinylation and GSH-strip recycling assay; representative western blot

rows.Finding description: Internalization of surface sortilin into CHO-S cells did not differ between apoE3 and apoE4 treatment (no significant difference); only the recycling step was affected.
rows.Finding quote: The detrimental effect of apoE4 was specific for the recycling step of the sorting path as the extent of internalization of sortilin (Figure S5B) or its ligand apoE (Fig- ures S5C, D) was not different comparing apoE3 and apoE4 treatment conditions
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (no change in sortilin internalization)
rows.Experimental system: CHO-S cells (murine sortilin) treated with apoE3 or apoE4; sortilin internalization assay (details in supplement)

rows.Finding description: PLA signal for sortilin-apoE complexes was scattered and vesicular throughout the cytoplasm with apoE3, but juxtamembrane with apoE4, suggesting altered intracellular trafficking of the receptor.
rows.Finding quote: Co-localization of sortilin with apoE3 was seen in a scattered vesicular pattern throughout the cytoplasm, whereas co-localization with apoE4 showed a distinct pattern close to the cell membrane (Figure 5A).
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (shift of sortilin/apoE complexes from dispersed vesicles to juxtamembrane compartments)
rows.Experimental system: CHO-S cells (murine sortilin); 24 h at 37 °C with 5 µg/mL myc-apoE3 or apoE4 produced in HEK293; proximity ligation assay

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 disruption of lipid metabolism, compared with APOE3, results in impaired late endosome/lysosome function.

rows.Finding description: APOE4-expressing cells showed enhanced lipid-droplet degradation by lipophagy in the paper's isoform comparison, opposing a uniform impairment of lysosomal autophagic degradation.
rows.Finding quote: Degradation of lipid droplets by lipophagy is enhanced in these APOE4-expressing cells, possibly in order to supply the necessary lipids to form autophagosomes.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (enhanced lipid-droplet degradation by lipophagy)
rows.Experimental system: Cultured APOE4-expressing cells in the paper's APOE3/APOE4 comparison. Cell species, cell type/source, age, lipid-loading conditions, assay method, and duration are not specified. The proposed supply of lipids for autophagosomes was not established experimentally in this text.
rows.Data location: Main text only, paragraph beginning “Having observed that APOE4 accumulates in lysosomes,” sentence 4. No figure panel or table is identified for lipid-droplet degradation.

rows.Finding description: APOE4-expressing cultured cells had higher LC3-II levels than the APOE3 comparison, consistent with altered autophagic flux.
rows.Finding quote: Similar to recent studies showing that APOE4 downregulates autophagy, we find higher levels of LC3-II in APOE4-expressing cells; this effect is not further modulated by bafilomycin A1 treatment, suggesting that there might be a late-stage block in autophagic flux at the level of the lysosome.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher LC3-II, suggesting impaired late-stage autophagic flux)
rows.Experimental system: Cultured APOE4-expressing cells in the paper's APOE3/APOE4 comparison. Cell species, cell type/source, age, assay method, and duration are not specified. LC3-II is a surrogate for autophagic status.
rows.Data location: Fig 1; “Similar to recent studies showing that APOE4 downregulates autophagy, we find higher levels of LC3-II in APOE4-expressing cells; this effect is not further modulated by bafilomycin A1 treatment, suggesting that there might be a late-stage block in autophagic flux at the level of the lysosome.”

rows.Finding description: Cultured cells expressing APOE4 showed APOE accumulation in enlarged lysosomes and late endosomes relative to the APOE3 condition summarized in Figure 1.
rows.Finding quote: Consistent with previous studies showing that expression of APOE4 damages lysosomal membrane integrity, dysregulates endo/lysosomal pH, and results in enlarged endosomes in various models, we found that APOE4 accumulates in enlarged lysosomes and late endosomes (Figure 1).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (APOE accumulation in enlarged lysosomes and late endosomes)
rows.Experimental system: Cultured cells studied using fluorescently tagged human APOE3 and APOE4 cell lines. Cell species, cell type/source, age, experimental duration, and measurement details are not specified. Human brain-cell identity and lipid-mediated causation are not established.
rows.Data location: Fig 1; main-text paragraph beginning “Late-onset AD is the most common form of dementia”

rows.Finding description: Proteomic analysis found reduced mitochondrial protein abundance in lysosomes from cells endocytosing APOE4, consistent with impaired mitochondrial delivery or mitophagy in the isoform comparison summarized by Figure 1.
rows.Finding quote: To further investigate how APOE4 may dysregulate autophagy, we performed proteomics analysis of lysosomes isolated from cells endocytosing APOE4, and found reduced levels of mitochondrial proteins, consistent with previous reports that APOE4 perturbs mitophagy.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4 internalization) -> (lower mitochondrial protein abundance in isolated lysosomes)
rows.Experimental system: Cultured cells endocytosing APOE4; isolated lysosomes analyzed by proteomics. Figure 1 frames the findings as APOE4 versus APOE3, but this sentence does not specify the proteomics comparator. Cell species, cell type/source, age, APOE preparation, dose, and exposure duration are not specified.
rows.Data location: Fig 1; “To further investigate how APOE4 may dysregulate autophagy, we performed proteomics analysis of lysosomes isolated from cells endocytosing APOE4, and found reduced levels of mitochondrial proteins, consistent with previous reports that APOE4 perturbs mitophagy.”

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 undergoes increased aggregation in the endo-lysosome compared with APOE3.

rows.Finding description: Table 1 lists a higher monomer-to-dimer association rate constant for apoE4 than for apoE3, 8.5×10³ versus 4.7×10³ M⁻¹s⁻¹. The authors used these previously determined association constants in the DMPC clearance fits.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher monomer-to-dimer association rate constant k+1)
rows.Experimental system: Full-length WT apoE4 and apoE3 in vitro. The pH 7.4 DMPC vesicle-clearance model used lipid-free self-association constants from ref. 35. The authors adjusted k−1 and k−2 in fitting the clearance data.

rows.Finding description: The dimer-to-monomer dissociation rate constant (k-1) was 6.4x10^-4 s-1 for apoE4 versus 5.4x10^-4 s-1 for apoE3; apoE4 dimers dissociate fastest, and the authors say this is the rate-limiting step for lipidation.
rows.Finding quote: Table 1 shows that the rate constants for dissociation of dimers to monomers (k-1) are different for the isoforms, being fastest for apoE4 and slowest for apoE2.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (faster dimer-to-monomer dissociation, k-1)
rows.Experimental system: Recombinant full-length human apoE4 vs apoE3, pH 7.4 HEPES buffer, 25 C, with DMPC SUVs (0.25 mg/mL); kinetic modeling with KinTek Explorer

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 undergoes increased aggregation in the endo-lysosome compared with APOE3.

rows.Finding description: Reducing SDS/PAGE of lipid-free recombinant apoE3 and apoE4 across HNE treatments showed a major approximately 36 kDa monomer band and a very faint approximately 72 kDa dimer band in both isoforms; no significant difference in dimerization was reported, and no between-isoform statistical test was supplied.
rows.Finding quote: In addition to the major band at ~ 36 kDa, a very faint minor band was noted ~ 72 kDa, corresponding to a dimer in all lanes for both apoE3 and apoE4.
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (no reported change in qualitative SDS-resistant dimer pattern)
rows.Experimental system: Human recombinant apoE3 and apoE4 expressed in Escherichia coli, examined lipid-free after treatment with varying HNE:apoE molar ratios for 2 h at 37 °C; reducing SDS/PAGE with Instant Blue staining. Cell-free experiment without endosomal or lysosomal localization.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 undergoes increased aggregation in the endo-lysosome compared with APOE3.

rows.Finding description: Fitting the FRET dilution kinetics to a monomer-dimer-tetramer model gave a lower monomer-dimer dissociation constant for recombinant ApoE4(A102C) than for ApoE3(C112S,A102C) (K12^-1 = 79 nM vs 119 nM). This means ApoE4 dimerizes with modestly higher affinity at neutral pH in vitro.
rows.Finding quote: Table 1 shows that the association and the dissociation rate constants for ApoE4, ApoE3 and ApoE2 are different.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower K12 dissociation constant, i.e. tighter dimerization of lipid-free apoE in vitro)
rows.Experimental system: Recombinant lipid-free human apoE4 (A102C) and apoE3 (C112S,A102C) labeled with Alexa488/Alexa546 (1:3); 15 uM stock diluted to 5-480 nM in 20 mM HEPES pH 7.4, 150 mM NaCl; intermolecular FRET kinetics over 1 h at 24 C, global fit in KinTek Explorer

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 undergoes increased aggregation in the endo-lysosome compared with APOE3.

rows.Finding description: For peptide 230–243, the model assigned 7 ± 1 wild-type ApoE3 amides and 8 ± 1 wild-type ApoE4 amides to the slow bin. Both monomeric mutants had 10 ± 1 in the fast bin. These counts support the authors’ qualitative conclusion of similar oligomerization properties. The paper reports no test of isoform equivalence.
rows.Finding summary: Wild-type ApoE3 and ApoE4 showed similar slow-bin counts for peptide 230–243.
rows.Experimental system: Recombinant human wild-type and monomeric-mutant (F257A/W264R/L279Q/V287E) ApoE3 and ApoE4; H/DX at pH 7.4, 25 °C, 0.5-60 min after dilution 4 µM to 400 nM; fixed-rate-constant binning fit (MathCAD)

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 disruption of lipid metabolism, compared with APOE3, results in impaired late endosome/lysosome function.

rows.Finding description: In human APOE-knockout cerebral organoids treated from day 90 for five days with apoE3- or apoE4-containing astrocyte-conditioned media, GCase protein abundance showed no significant difference across treatments, using five pooled samples per group with three organoids per sample.
rows.Finding quote: Western blotting showed that the addition of exogenous astrocytic media containing apoE2 and apoE3 isoforms reduced the level of Plin2 in the APOE−/− cerebral organoids compared to the media from Apoe-KO astrocytes or containing apoE4, although there was no effect on the levels of EEA1, LAMP1, GCase, LIMP1, αSyn and p-αSyn in the RIPA fraction (Fig. 4b–i).
rows.Finding summary: (exogenous astrocytic apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (no change in lysosomal enzyme GCase protein abundance in APOE-knockout cerebral organoids)
rows.Experimental system: Human iPSC-derived APOE−/− cerebral organoids containing neurons and astrocytes; five-day treatment starting at day 90 with conditioned media from immortalized astrocytes derived from human APOE3- or APOE4-targeted-replacement mice; equivalent apoE concentrations across isoform treatments; RIPA-fraction GCase Western blotting normalized to β-actin; enzyme activity was not measured in this panel; Apoe-knockout and APOE2 conditioned media were additional groups; three independent differentiation batches.
